reviewer: Independent Astra editorial and related-guide relevance review
decision: All 16 recommendations and all 499 existing associations pass substantive editorial and relevance review on the pinned inputs. Apply the approved association fingerprints and four supplied reason replacements to the ledger before its final quality gate. This report does not certify deployment or substitute for the parent’s technical checks.
reviewMethod: Read all 16 recommendation/pre-draft/editorial records, all 19 complete changed rendered article or service/tool main texts, all six new worksheets and four extended downloads. For service/tool HTML, excluded scripts, styles and global navigation from the main-text read.

Read each of the five complete current guide articles and reviewed the before/after textual changes. For every one of the 499 associations, read its existing label and reason alongside its full unchanged local decision paragraph and decision title, then assessed the connection against the current guide.

Retained prior independent full-location-purpose findings where unchanged and still supported. Consulted complete lead, scope and planning-table fields for nine selected records, including the removed-example and former-target wording cases. This was not a new read of all 499 full scope/planning-table records or a re-research of unchanged business sources.

Used the repository’s exported locationPurposeFingerprint and guidePurposeFingerprint functions to confirm all 499 unchanged location-purpose fingerprints, all 499 prior guide fingerprints against their group and all five current rendered guide fingerprints. Hash verification bound the semantic decisions to inputs; it did not generate the relevance judgments.

Read the complete existing manufacturing RFQ and website-launch-checklist articles for overlap, and used the complete content-template article for the content-guide comparison. Checked the final industrial RFQ source and rendered paragraph after the missing connection was repaired.

Verified all 52 manifest source/package/rendered-file byte hashes before writing this report. No builds, full test runs, browser checks, external business-source queries or ledger edits were performed by this reviewer.

recommendationReviews.title: Choose an SEO plan from the work that needs doing
recommendationReviews.evidence: Three fictional selection cases distinguish Improve at $400/month with one completed improvement, Grow at $800/month with two connected improvements plus a separate reuse piece, and Keep Running at $150/month with supplied edits and checks. Ready inputs, baseline eligibility and no outcome guarantees remain explicit.

recommendationReviews.title: Match everyday website tasks to the right support owner
recommendationReviews.evidence: Five everyday requests distinguish supplied photo/text changes, new-page improvement work, checking a failed form versus repairing it, checking a booking link versus configuring a provider, and CMS restore work requiring a host or specialist. The maintenance-cost guide preserves the same task boundaries and separate provider bills.

recommendationReviews.title: Connect the existing cost estimator and ROI calculator with worked scenarios
recommendationReviews.evidence: Payments and ROI pages connect a hypothetical Launch-plus-care budget of $1,400 + 12 x $150 = $3,200 and an existing-site baseline-plus-three-Improve-months budget of $399 + 3 x $400 = $1,599. Unknown provider costs remain unresolved, full-budget and incremental analysis are distinguished, and no scenario is a contract minimum or result deadline.

recommendationReviews.title: Show why two website budgets differ using equal-scope examples
recommendationReviews.evidence: The matched-proposal example holds a six-page site and customer task constant, then compares writing, forms, search work, redirects, editing, ownership, provider costs and reviews. Missing supplier prices remain unanswered rather than becoming invented market averages or false zero costs.

recommendationReviews.title: Demonstrate the included writing process from business facts to a service page
recommendationReviews.evidence: The service-page example and annotated content-template example derive a deck-repair page from rough owner facts, show what was clarified and identify the owner approvals still needed. Complete writing remains part of the agreed website scope; no separate copywriting offer or unsupported credential, price or result is added.

recommendationReviews.title: Add two complete trade briefs to the contractor resource
recommendationReviews.evidence: The HVAC replacement and roofing assessment briefs each identify the customer, scope, page plan, evidence, six initial fields and receipt checks. They preserve professional assessment, optional timing, truthful response expectations and separate decisions for uploads, dispatch, portals and automatic prices.

recommendationReviews.title: Choose the fields for a useful quote-request form
recommendationReviews.evidence: Three six-field examples cover a project inquiry, scheduled service and initial B2B request. Keep/defer/remove reasoning, required versus optional fields, unknown quantity, receipt semantics and receiving-owner checks make the article and worksheet usable without presenting six fields as a universal rule.

recommendationReviews.title: Write FAQ answers that help customers choose
recommendationReviews.evidence: Six weak-to-useful FAQ examples cover price, fit, coverage, preparation, timing and next action. Each relies on actual owner facts; the guide explains service-page placement versus shared FAQ use and avoids unsupported rich-result or conversion promises.

recommendationReviews.title: Announce a website launch with a useful customer message
recommendationReviews.evidence: Email, social and on-site announcement examples lead with an actual customer task and a checked destination. Placeholder links are marked, operational claims remain bounded and each channel requires its own owner, audience and publication approval. The worksheet supplies editable drafts and review fields.

recommendationReviews.title: Make inquiry confirmations clear about the next step
recommendationReviews.evidence: Project, quote and pending-booking confirmations distinguish verified receipt, stored record, notification processing, receiving inbox and accepted work. The guide and worksheet include failure and uncertain-status handling, approved response arrangements and no invented reference or booking status.

recommendationReviews.title: Connect a redesign RFP to evidence and acceptance checks
recommendationReviews.evidence: Three requirements connect useful URLs, inquiry routing and opening-hours updates to evidence, provider response, dependencies, acceptance and a named owner. The extended existing brief preserves source-file editing and optional-care boundaries; unresolved access is recorded instead of guessed as passing.

recommendationReviews.title: Build a case-study page from evidence a business can support
recommendationReviews.evidence: The case-study framework and completed fictional process example separate problem, constraints, roles, work, completion evidence, optional outcomes and permissions. They remain useful without measured growth, avoid fabricated client records and distinguish observed change from causal attribution.

recommendationReviews.title: Show how a monthly SEO report leads to the next decision
recommendationReviews.evidence: The completed fictional monthly report identifies the task, approval, version/date, publication checks, observation windows, unavailable measurements and next decision. The missing-Search-Console-access variant asserts no performance change; click events remain distinct from verified suitable inquiries.

recommendationReviews.title: Add a content-migration example to the existing URL checklist
recommendationReviews.evidence: The migration guide adds keep, rewrite, merge and retire decisions with factual review, image permissions, owner and verification. The extended existing CSV preserves equivalent destinations, meaningful retained content and 404/410 handling for a genuinely retired offer rather than redirecting everything home.

recommendationReviews.title: Plan an industrial website around capability evidence and an RFQ
recommendationReviews.evidence: The industrial site plan connects buyer fit, approved capabilities, document revision/ownership, project evidence and a human-reviewed RFQ. It avoids invented tolerances, credentials, capacity or a new commercial package. The final rendered #rfq paragraph now links the existing manufacturing RFQ guide and worksheet for drawing revisions, document receipt and responsibility.

recommendationReviews.title: Turn service-area guidance into a territory evidence worksheet
recommendationReviews.evidence: The North/South fictional territory comparison demonstrates both a potentially useful separate explanation and a case that belongs on the existing service page. It records owner facts, source/date, purpose and review ownership, rejects invented offices/local outcomes and requires comparing the complete answer before creating a page.

Six decision categories, weak/better example, fact source, approval and review trigger match the article.

offerFidelity.evidence: Prices and allowances match the pinned offer catalog: Launch $1,400, Focused $2,350, Signature $3,700; 6/15/30-page caps; one/two/two simple forms with up to six agreed fields; baseline $399 when required; care $150; Improve $400 with one improvement; Grow $800 with two connected improvements and separate reuse piece. Source-file editing, provider bills, unsupported CMS work, optional ongoing service and approval boundaries remain clear.

fictionalExamplesAndClaims.evidence: Worked businesses, messages, project/report records and territory labels are clearly fictional or hypothetical. They add concrete decisions, fields, approvals and acceptance checks without fabricated client work, credentials, technical specifications, testimonials or measured outcomes.

calculations: $1,400 + 12 x $150 = $3,200 studio spend in the illustrative Launch-plus-care year.
$399 + 3 x $400 = $1,599 for the illustrative baseline and three Improve months.

The existing ROI illustration uses $2,350 + 12 x $180 = $4,510 cost; 4 extra inquiries x 25% x 12 = 12 extra jobs; 12 x $500 = $6,000 contribution; $1,490 net and approximately 33% ROI. Steady monthly contribution after recurring cost is $320, giving approximately 7.3-month initial-cost recovery.
costAndRoi.evidence: Direct job contribution is distinguished from revenue; available evidence and unknown costs remain explicit; existing revenue is not automatically attributed to the website; timing, seasonality and input assumptions limit interpretation. No return, demand or result deadline is promised.

noNewCommercialOffer.evidence: Writing is explained as an existing package inclusion. Industrial content is a planning guide for the existing website service, with engineering review, restricted libraries, catalogues and system connections separately assessed.

overlapReview.evidence: Industrial planning addresses the site-wide buyer decision and approval of capability/specification content. Quote-request fields address the minimum first conversation. The existing manufacturing RFQ resource handles drawing revisions, attachments, missing specifications and production-review states; the final industrial paragraph now directs that deeper task there.

The content template assembles general page facts and owner notes. FAQ examples teach answer selection and placement. Case studies assemble attributable project evidence and permissions. Shared fictional deck-repair context develops different outputs without creating duplicate generic service articles.

The existing checklist governs launch readiness, accounts, release, recovery and live checks. The announcement resource governs the customer message, channel, destination and publication approval after those checks.

guideReviews.change: Replaces the shorter bathroom/exterior illustrations with complete HVAC replacement and roofing assessment briefs; retains accepted-work, project evidence, coverage, preparation and inquiry principles.
guideReviews.relevance: All 166 local decisions still concern actual service scope, project roles, useful examples or assessment preparation. guideReviews.change: Replaces the earlier single cleaning example with a two-territory decision record contrasting a potentially useful explanation with an existing-page answer.
guideReviews.relevance: The premise/location/service-reach distinction and current address-level, service and scheduling limits remain explicit. Those sections still directly support the Broward, Calhoun and Leon decisions; the new example reinforces avoiding unsupported area pages.

guideReviews.change: Adds a content inventory before the URL map, covering keep, rewrite, merge and retire decisions, facts, permissions and owners.
guideReviews.relevance: The guide still directly supports Buchanan County preserving useful old Southern Gap routes and the correct property identity through a rebrand. The new inventory makes retained property-specific content more explicit.
